title: Hilton Global Foundation and Hilton UK Foundation Back UK Charities and Organisations with Nearly £900,000 to Help Young People Get Ahead
summary: Twelve UK charities and organisations are benefitting from funding from the Hilton Global Foundation and Hilton UK Foundation.
body_markdown:
Listen to this article


0:00


- **Hilton UK Foundation granted £600,000 to 11 charities and organisations focusing on helping young people gain skills, experience and routes into work, including Springboard, Team Domenica and The Burnt Chef Project.**
- **Hilton Global Foundation this year provided £260,000 to Felix, the UK’s leading food redistribution charity, to fully fund its Commis Chef Apprenticeship Programme.**
- **Apprentices from the Felix Programme put their training into practice at Hilton London Canary Wharf, gaining their first experience in a professional hotel kitchen.**
- **In 2026 Hilton and its charity partners are supporting more than 4,000 young people with hospitality industry experience.**


**LONDON** – Twelve UK charities and organisations are benefitting from funding from the[Hilton Global Found](https://hiltonglobalfoundation.hilton.com/)[a](https://hiltonglobalfoundation.hilton.com/)[tion](https://hiltonglobalfoundation.hilton.com/) and Hilton UK Foundation, with a particular focus on those helping young people gain skills, experience and routes into work.


This year, Hilton Global Foundation, Hilton’s global philanthropic arm, is supporting **Felix** , the UK’s leading food rescue charity and a long-standing Hilton partner, to power its Commis Chef Apprenticeship Programme. The goal is to help apprentices gain recognised qualifications and practical hospitality experience as they work towards careers across the sector. Last week, apprentices put their training into practice at Hilton London Canary Wharf, gaining their first experience in a professional hotel kitchen. More broadly the Foundation supports organisations across the globe working to expand career opportunity, advance community resilience and make the world better to travel.


Separately, through its fundraising efforts, the Hilton UK Foundation, an independent UK charity, has granted £600,000 to 11 UK organisations, with an aim to support causes helping future generations. Grantees include **Team Domenica** , which helps young people with learning disabilities move into work through specialist training and employer partnerships, as well as **Only A Pavement Away** , **Fair Shot,** **The Right Course** and the **Down Syndrome Association’s WorkFit programme** .


Stephen Cassidy, senior vice president, UK & Ireland, Hilton and chairman, Hilton UK Foundation, said, "Hospitality has the power to open doors for people who might otherwise be overlooked. At a time when too many young people are struggling to gain the experience employers are looking for, the Hilton Global Foundation and Hilton UK Foundation are helping organisations create practical pathways into work through apprenticeships, training, mentoring and hands-on workplace experience. By helping people develop skills, confidence and employability, they are unlocking potential in communities across the UK and creating opportunities that can change lives."


### **Supporting 4,000 young people into work**


-
-


Chef Neeshal and Felix Apprentice Chefs Maisie and Zack at Hilton London Canary Wharf


Alongside the work of the Hilton Global Foundation and Hilton UK Foundation, Hilton is on track to support more than 4,000 young people across the UK this year through work placements, careers events, mock interviews, workshops and hotel visits. The activity is delivered with local schools, colleges and organisations, as well as partners backed by the Hilton Global Foundation, including the UK hospitality careers charity **Springboard** . Together with Springboard, Hilton will also hold an event in early 2027 to help hundreds of students, parents, teachers and careers advisers explore hospitality careers.


Hilton's support comes as nearly one million young people across the UK are not in education, employment or training. But it’s clear that hospitality can help. Hilton-commissioned research found that more than four in five of business leaders agreed hospitality helps people develop soft skills valued in other industries, while 76% would be more likely to hire someone with hospitality experience over an otherwise equally qualified candidate. Eighty-one per cent of business leaders also believe young people struggle to gain the experience employers expect without access to entry-level roles.


### **Felix Case Studies – Commis Chef Apprenticeship Programme**


-
-


As part of Felix’s Commis Chef Apprenticeship Programme, Zack Isse and Maisie Moore recently gained their first experience in a professional hotel kitchen at Hilton London Canary Wharf, working alongside the hotel’s culinary team and putting their training into practice Zack Isse, 24, joined Felix's chef apprenticeship programme after struggling to gain the experience needed to start a career in hospitality: “Before joining the programme, I had a passion for food but didn’t have the experience or confidence to take the next step. Now I’m training as a chef, learning new skills every day and building a future in hospitality. Working in a busy Hilton kitchen gave me a real sense of what the job involves and made me even more determined to succeed. There are lots of people with the passion to do well who just need the chance to learn and show what they can do.”


Before joining the programme, 21-year-old Maisie Moore had never held a paid job and was unsure what her future might look like: “Over the past six months, I’ve gained confidence, developed practical skills and discovered how many opportunities hospitality can offer. Working in a busy Hilton kitchen was a real highlight and pushed me outside my comfort zone. It showed me how much there is to learn in hospitality and the different directions a career in the industry could take me.”


##### FAQ: Hilton Global Foundation and Hilton UK Foundation Back UK Charities and Organisations with Nearly £900,000 to Help Young People Get Ahead


Hilton Global Foundation granted £260,000 to Felix, UK’s leading food redistribution charity while the Hilton UK Foundation provided £600,000 to 11 UK charities and organisations helping young people, jobseekers and people facing barriers to work gain training, experience and support into employment.


Hilton’s research found that nearly one million young people in the UK are not in education, employment or training, and one in four unemployed NEETs say lack of experience is their biggest barrier to work. It also found that 81% of business leaders believe young people struggle to gain the experience employers expect without access to entry-level roles. By supporting charities that offer training, mentoring and time in real workplaces, Hilton UK Foundation and Hilton Global Foundation are helping more people build the confidence and experience employers look for.


The following organisations are receiving support this year across employment, inclusion, wellbeing and environmental programmes.


**Felix:** Felix was founded in 2026 following the merger of The Felix Project and FareShare. The charity rescues good-to-eat surplus food, that would otherwise go to waste and gets it to more than 8,000 community organisations across the UK, reaching over 1.5 million people. Through funding from the Hilton Global Foundation, Hilton supports both the charity’s food redistribution work and its Commis Chef Apprenticeship Programme, which helps vulnerable young people gain qualifications, kitchen experience and routes into long-term employment.


**Springboard:** Springboard is the UK’s leading hospitality careers charity, helping people from disadvantaged backgrounds build careers in the industry. Its Destination Hospitality programme provides training, qualifications, work placements and mentoring for young people and adults facing barriers such as unemployment, low income and mental health challenges. Funding will help more people facing barriers to work access training, qualifications, mentoring and employment opportunities across the hospitality sector.


**Team Domenica:** Team Domenica is a Brighton-based charity helping young people with learning disabilities and autism to move into work through specialist training and employer partnerships. Its two-year programme gives participants real-world experience, including work placements and internships with local employers, more than half of them in hospitality. Support from the Hilton UK Foundation will help expand employer partnerships and create more inclusive job opportunities.


**The Burnt Chef Project:** The Burnt Chef Project is a global social enterprise supporting mental health and wellbeing across hospitality. Through free eLearning, college workshops and a 24/7 confidential text support service, it provides practical help for workers and students in a high-pressure industry. Funding from the Hilton UK Foundation will help expand its services across the UK, increasing access to support and helping build a healthier, more resilient hospitality workforce.


**Only A Pavement Away:** Only A Pavement Away connects individuals experiencing homelessness, prison leavers and other barriers to employment with jobs in hospitality. Through training, 121 support and employer partnerships, the charity helps people build stable careers and greater independence. Funding will support more learning and development opportunities, helping more people move into long-term work.


**Down Syndrome Association’s WorkFit programme:** The Down Syndrome Association’s WorkFit programme supports people who have Down’s syndrome secure meaningful, paid work by matching candidates with inclusive employers and providing advice, resources, training and ongoing workplace support. It also works with businesses to remove barriers and enhance accessibility to support participants to build confidence, increase independence, develop professionally and successfully navigate the world of work.


**Fair Shot:** Fair Shot helps young adults with learning disabilities move into work through immersive hospitality training at its Covent Garden social enterprise café. The charity also works with employers to improve inclusive hiring and create lasting job opportunities. Funding will expand training and employment support for 45 young adults with learning disabilities in 2026.


**The Right Course:** The Right Course uses hospitality training to help people in prison gain skills, confidence and qualifications that improve their chances of finding work after release. By turning prison staff restaurants into training environments, and supporting graduates through the gates and into employment, the charity gives learners real-world experience and supports a route away from reoffending.


**Debate Mate:** Debate Mate helps young people build confidence, communication and critical thinking skills through programmes in schools and communities. Funding will support work with students in disadvantaged areas, helping them strengthen employability skills, raise aspirations and explore future careers, including in hospitality.


**Cameron’s Companions:** Cameron’s Companions provides vital mental health support to men and boys experiencing suicidal thoughts and emotional distress. Its services offer rapid access to counselling without the need for GP referrals, helping individuals access professional support quickly and reducing barriers to early intervention. Funding will help expand access to these services and reach more people in need.


**Sunnyside Rural Trust:** Sunnyside Rural Trust offers adults with learning disabilities opportunities to acquire skills in various horticulture and retail activities. The organisation believes in empowering individuals to fulfil their potential, benefiting not only themselves but also the broader community and environment. Funding will help redevelop a rural cabin into a community wellbeing and education hub, creating a welcoming space for learning, social connection and skills development for people with learning disabilities, families and carers.


**4ocean Foundation:** 4ocean Foundation removes plastic pollution from the ocean, rivers, and coastlines while supporting healthier marine ecosystems and coastal communities. Funding will support its Bali Rainy Season Rapid Response programme, intercepting plastic during peak monsoon periods before it breaks down into harmful microplastics and disperses into the sea. Through global education and awareness initiatives, the Foundation also inspires behaviour change and empowers communities to take action for a healthier planet.

## About Hilton

Dedicated to fulfilling its founding vision to fill the earth with the light and warmth of hospitality, Hilton has welcomed over 4 billion guests in its more than 100-year history. Named as the No. 1 World’s Best Workplace by Great Place to Work and Fortune, Hilton aims to create the best culture for its 500,000 team members around the world. Hilton has introduced industry-leading technology enhancements to improve the guest experience, including Digital Key Share, automated complimentary room upgrades and the ability to book confirmed connecting rooms. Through the award-winning guest loyalty program Hilton Honors, the more than 270 million Hilton Honors members who book directly with Hilton can earn Points for hotel stays and experiences money can't buy. ## About Hilton Global Foundation


The Hilton Global Foundation is Hilton’s primary philanthropic arm, supporting the company’s Travel with Purpose strategy to drive positive impact and deliver lasting value to the people, hotels and communities where we all live, work and stay. Through grants and partnerships, the Foundation invests in programs that advance destination stewardship, foster career development and strengthen community resilience. Since 2019, it has contributed more than $25 million to organizations around the world and positively impacted millions of lives. Learn more at[hiltonglobalfoundation.hilton.com](https://hiltonglobalfoundation.hilton.com/) .


---


## About Hilton UK Foundation


At the beginning of 2022, Hilton launched the Hilton UK Foundation, an independent charity registered in England and Wales (charity number 1198428). This foundation supports Hilton’s overall mission to spread the light and warmth of hospitality in the United Kingdom. In the UK, Hilton has a long history of partnering with organizations whose priorities align with our own aim to create a better world to travel and whose priorities help us achieve our 2030 goals. ****
